title: Strategic Partnership QBR Slate & Renewal Ask Matrix (Standard + Enterprise)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working draft provides a compact, slide-first QBR slate (aka slide order + speaker notes) and a practical Renewal Ask Matrix that CSMs can use for both Standard (self-serve / SMB / mid-market) and Enterprise customers. The goal is to make each QBR repeatable, measurable, and aligned to the commercial outcome we need for renewal or expansion.

How to use this file:
- Pick the slate variant (Standard or Enterprise) depending on customer tier and meeting length.
- Use the Ask Matrix to define 1 primary ask + 2 backup asks (tiered by friction level).
- After the meeting, update the Renewal Tracker row and send the tailored one-pager follow-up.

Slide slate (Standard customer, 30 minutes total)
1) Cover & Agenda (1 min)
  - Title: Customer name QBR — YYYY-MM-DD
  - Purpose line: 30 min — health, usage, and a single renewal ask
  - Speaker note: Confirm we have the right attendees and outcome (renew or next meeting).

2) Quarterly Snapshot (4 min)
  - Top metrics: daily active users, API calls, token consumption, error rate
  - Trend visual: 90-day sparkline for adoption and cost per MAU
  - Speaker note: Keep to 3 data points; connect to customer goals.

3) Wins & Product Value (6 min)
  - 3 bullet successes with evidence (customer quote, metric uplift, saved hours)
  - Short demo or screenshot if one exists
  - Speaker note: Frame wins as business outcomes, not features.

4) Risk Signals & Mitigation (5 min)
  - Highlight top 3 risks (drop in usage, increased latency, integration debt)
  - Proposed mitigations and owner for each
  - Speaker note: Be explicit about ask from customer (e.g., commit to an integration sprint).

5) Renewal Ask (6 min)
  - Use the Ask Matrix to present 1 primary ask + two reduced-scope options
  - Pricing reminder and contract expiration date
  - Speaker note: Ask for a decision timeline; capture next action.

6) Next steps & Contacts (3 min)
  - Clear owner/action/date for 3-week and 90-day checkpoints
  - Thank you + exec sponsor copy list

Appendix: Quick troubleshooting playbook (one page)
  - Common issues and where to escalate (SRE, Solutions Eng, Billing)

Slide slate (Enterprise customer, 60–90 minutes)
1) Executive Summary & Purpose (5 min)
  - One-slide from Redwood exec or the CSM summarizing strategic alignment
  - Meeting outcome options: renewal, expansion, roadmap sync

2) Business Outcomes & ROI (10–15 min)
  - Quantified impact (time saved, revenue influenced, defect reduction)
  - Attribution methodology (how numbers were derived)
  - Speaker note: Bring a customer success story or case study contrast.

3) Adoption & Usage Deep Dive (10 min)
  - Feature adoption cohorts, latency impact on key paths, cost breakdown by team
  - Heatmap: teams by API usage + anomaly callouts

4) Roadmap Alignment & Product Commitments (10–15 min)
  - Two-way roadmap: what Redwood plans and what customer prioritized
  - Milestones and acceptance criteria for joint initiatives

5) Risk & Compliance Review (10 min)
  - Security findings, performance SLOs, audit trail summary for Private deployments
  - Remediation timeline and owning teams

6) Commercial Review & Ask Matrix (15 min)
  - Renewal options, recommended seat/throughput tier, and expansion playbook
  - Negotiation levers: term, volume discounts, professional services credits

7) Decisioning & Next Steps (5–10 min)
  - Formal decision owner, timeline, trial or pilot extensions if needed
  - Post-meeting deliverables: contract draft, implementation checklist, governance cadence

Renewal Ask Matrix (how to build it quickly during prep)
- Columns: Ask label | Primary value to customer | CS friction level (Low/Med/High) | Price delta (vs current) | Required Redwood action | Customer decision timeline
- Example rows (as text):
  1) "Auto-renew 12mo @ current tier" | "Predictable cost, no product change" | Low | +0% | None beyond billing | Decision by end of QBR week
  2) "Upgrade to Reserved Dedicated (6 GPUs)" | "Guaranteed throughput for peak traffic" | High | +40% | Migration plan + SRE runbook | Decision in 2 weeks with exec sign-off
  3) "Add Optimize bundle (monitoring + quality alerts)" | "Lower unit cost and regression alerts" | Medium | +12% | Setup & eval prompts | 30-day pilot decision

Guidelines for picking asks
- Standard customers: prefer low-friction asks tied to adoption (usage increase, lock-in via 12mo renewal).
- Enterprise: prioritize business outcomes and mitigation of operational risks; be prepared to exchange PS credits or roadmap commitments.
- Always have a binary primary ask and two fallbacks; record the expected decision owner and timeline pre-meeting.

Renewal tracker (compact row format for the one-line per customer table)
- Fields (one-line): Customer | Renewal date | Current ARR | Health score (0-100) | Primary ask | Decision owner | Next action & date | Risk flags
- Example entry as single line text:
  Acme Corp | 2026-06-15 | $185k | 78 | 12mo auto-renew @ current tier | VP Product, Sarah J. | Send proposal draft by 2026-05-01 | Flags: latency spikes in May

Pre-QBR prep checklist (CSM to complete two weeks prior)
- Verify data sources (billing, telemetry, SLOs) and refresh dashboards
- Run a short adoption audit with Solutions Eng: top 3 friction points
- Draft the Ask Matrix and share with AE for commercial guidance
- Prepare one-pager exec summary tailored to the sponsor

Post-QBR follow-up templates (one-pager variants)
- Standard one-pager: 1-page PDF summarizing decisions, primary ask, 3 next steps, and signature line for AE
- Enterprise one-pager: 2-page pack with ROI appendix, implementation timeline, and legal/finance checklist

Triage flow for indicated risks (quick playbook)
- If usage drops >25% month-over-month: schedule 1:1 technical health call within 3 business days (owner: CSM + Solutions Eng)
- If SLO breach reported: engage SRE runbook and create incident ticket; communicate SLA impact to customer execs within 24 hours
- If renewal at risk (health <60): escalate to Head of CS and AE for commercial rescue call within 48 hours

Communication cadences and templates
- Pre-QBR: invite exec sponsor + day-of logistics email 7 days prior; reminder 48 hours prior
- Post-QBR: deliver one-pager within 48 hours, include action owners, and set 30/60/90 day follow-ups in calendar

Variations and playbook notes (unique ideas not in other templates)
- "Reverse QBR" micro-format: CSM asks the customer to present 10 minutes on their biggest blocker — drives ownership and surfaces cross-org issues early
- "Guardrail ask": propose a 90-day trial of a higher tier, with a metrics-based rollback clause (helps lower negotiation friction)
- "SLA-as-a-Service" pitch for customers with compliance needs: combine Private deployment baseline with monthly SLO review and remediation credits

Speaker tips and rhetorical scripts
- Opening (exec): "We're here to make sure Redwood is a predictable, measurable part of your roadmap. Today I want two outcomes: understand your ops picture and agree on a next step toward renewal or expansion."
- Framing a risk: "We see a pattern in the telemetry that could cause outages during your next launch window. Our proposal mitigates this risk in X, Y, Z ways — what tradeoffs do you want us to consider?"

Checklist for the CSM bundle to attach to the final deliverable
- One-pager (tailored)
- Contract or quote draft (AE)
- Implementation / migration runbook (Solutions Eng)
- SLO dashboard snapshot and anomaly log (SRE)

Open questions & decisions to finalize in this draft
- Standardized health scoring methodology across products (CS + Product to finalize)
- Template for executive ROI calculations (Finance input needed)
- How far in advance should RDW execs join Enterprise QBRs (policy suggestion: >$250k ARR or >50% churn risk)

Notes to self / next edits
- Add sample slide exports (PNG) for the appendix
- Coordinate with Legal on the rollback clause language
- Create a short Playbook checklist card for the CSM mobile app
